title: Epilogue. The Science Behind the Machine

blocks.text: This book is a novel, a sequel to *The Daughter of Two Worlds*, *Letters from the Stars* and *The Children of the Earth*. Aya, Andrés, Lía, the clone, Nexum, the two-circle machine and the transfer of a body, particle by particle, from one world to another are fiction. What follows is not. Here we separate, as carefully as we can, what already existed in 2026 (with date and source) from what still belongs to the realm of speculation or dream. Nothing written in these pages replaces the judgement of a healthcare professional.

blocks.text: **Energy is neither created nor destroyed: it is transformed.** On 23 July 1847, Hermann von Helmholtz presented to the Physical Society of Berlin the memoir *Über die Erhaltung der Kraft* (“On the Conservation of Force”), published that same year in Berlin by G. Reimer (https://www.deutschestextarchiv.de/book/show/helmholtz_erhaltung_1847). In it he formulated, systematically, the principle that “force” (what we now call energy) is conserved: it does not appear out of nothing or disappear, but changes form. Other researchers of that same decade, among them Julius Robert von Mayer and James Prescott Joule, had reached related ideas by different routes. That principle is today the first law of thermodynamics. It holds for a body that cools, for a wave that breaks, for a cup that falls. It does not say, by itself, that a man is the same after a journey, nor that a while of a life can be reconstructed. It says only that, in an isolated system, the energy balance is maintained.

blocks.text: **Information cannot be copied or transmitted without limit or without cost.** In July 1948, *The Bell System Technical Journal* published the first part of “A Mathematical Theory of Communication” by Claude E. Shannon (https://doi.org/10.1002/j.1538-7305.1948.tb01338.x). Shannon showed that a communication channel has a maximum capacity: more information than the channel allows cannot be passed through it reliably. In July 1961, the *IBM Journal of Research and Development* published “Irreversibility and Heat Generation in the Computing Process” by Rolf Landauer (https://doi.org/10.1147/rd.53.0183). Landauer argued that erasing a bit of information has a minimum physical energy cost, of the order of *kT* per irreversible operation (more precisely *kT* ln 2), where *T* is the temperature. Information, in the real world, is not a free vapour: it is tied to a medium, a channel and heat. That neither authorises nor describes the instantaneous transfer of a human body. It does prevent us from dreaming, with any rigour, that “everything a person is” could be copied or sent without paying a physical price and without a limit on what fits in a message.

blocks.text: **An unknown quantum state cannot be cloned.** On 28 October 1982, *Nature* published “A single quantum cannot be cloned” by W. K. Wootters and W. H. Zurek (https://www.nature.com/articles/299802a0). The paper shows that no device can perfectly copy the unknown quantum state of a system: if it could, one could measure exactly quantities that quantum mechanics does not allow to be known at the same time. Independently, Dennis Dieks reached an equivalent conclusion in “Communication by EPR devices”, *Physics Letters A*, 15 November 1982 (https://doi.org/10.1016/0375-9601(82)90084-6). This no-cloning theorem is not a company rule: it is a prohibition of physics. In the novel, Nexum's attempt to assemble “without loss”, leaving the original in its place, fails. That, in the realm of quantum states, matches what these papers had already established.

blocks.text: **Quantum teleportation transfers a state, not a body, and the original of that state is lost.** On 29 March 1993, *Physical Review Letters* published “Teleporting an unknown quantum state via dual classical and Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen channels” by Charles H. Bennett, Gilles Brassard, Claude Crépeau, Richard Jozsa, Asher Peres and William K. Wootters (https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.70.1895). The protocol shows how the unknown quantum state of one particle can be reconstructed in another, distant one, using an entangled pair and a classical message. The matter of the first particle is not transferred. Its state is. The starting state is destroyed: if it were preserved, there would be a copy, and the no-cloning theorem forbids that. A classical channel is also needed, which is why this procedure does not allow information to be sent faster than light.

blocks.text: On 11 December 1997, *Nature* published “Experimental quantum teleportation” by Dik Bouwmeester, Jian-Wei Pan, Klaus Mattle, Manfred Eibl, Harald Weinfurter and Anton Zeilinger (https://www.nature.com/articles/37539). The team demonstrated the protocol in the laboratory, teleporting the polarisation state of a photon. On 9 August 2017, *Nature* published online “Ground-to-satellite quantum teleportation” by Ji-Gang Ren and a large Chinese team, with Jian-Wei Pan as corresponding author (https://www.nature.com/articles/nature23675). In that work, the state of a photon was teleported from the ground to the Micius satellite, over hundreds of kilometres. These are still states of particles that already exist at the destination, not people, not tissues, not a cup that appears with its crack.

blocks.text: **Nobody has teleported a body, or a cell, or an everyday object.** In 2026, quantum teleportation is still the transfer of a state (almost always that of a photon, sometimes that of an atom or a small system) to a system that was already on the other side. There is no machine that breaks a man down into particles and puts him back together, whole, in a warehouse near El Estacio or in a hangar on another world. There is no published and reproduced protocol that reconstructs the arrangement of an organism's atoms, nor any measure of the information needed to describe one that would fit, in practice, through a channel. Conserving a body's energy is not enough: one would also have to conserve and transmit its organisation, with a fidelity that known physics does not offer for an object of that scale, and which the no-cloning theorem prevents from being obtained by way of a perfect copy of the complete quantum state.

blocks.text: The machine in this novel is therefore a premise of fiction. It has been written so as deliberately not to contradict what is known: it does not duplicate, it does not leave an original and a faithful copy, it does not travel faster than a classical message in the sense of the 1993 teleportation, and it does not give back the whiles, only (were it to work) a material order. That consistency is a mark of respect for physics, not proof that transferring a fisherman is possible.

blocks.text: Andrés crosses and wonders whether the one who arrives is the same. The one who searches arrives, sits down, leaves. Aya does not step into the circle. Lía asks questions and does not correct the hollow. The science of 2026 can say that energy is conserved, that an unknown quantum state cannot be cloned, that real teleportation transfers states and destroys the starting one, and that information has a cost and a ceiling. It cannot yet tell us whether a man who was undone and made again would be, for his household, the same, nor what we should do with the whiles that do not travel. That question is ethical and philosophical, not technical, and no paper will settle it. That is why, on this shore, it is left open, beside a cup, and the asking goes on.
